newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Increased calls lift PLDT 9-mth net 32 pct.
newsitem.headline: Increased calls lift PLDT 9-mth net 32 pct.

text.p: Increased call volumes lifted the net income of Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co Inc by 32.0 percent in the first nine months of the year, the company said on Wednesday.

It reported a net income of 4.670 billion pesos in the first three quarters of 1996, against last year's 4.693 billion pesos which included a 1.154 billion peso extraordinary gain from the sale of its stake in its subsidiary Pilipino Telephone Corp last year.
"Without this unusual gain in 1995, net income in 1996 would be 32.0 percent higher over that of 1995," the company said in a statement.
Operating revenues jumped by 15.6 percent to 21.136 billion from 18.276 billion pesos a year ago.
Revenues from local calls rose by 16.7 percent to 5.286 billion pesos from 4.528 billion for the same period last year because the company installed more lines during the period.
As of September 30, the company had a total of 1,364,064 lines in service against 1,096,604 last year.

"National long distance network revenues, which comprised 17.5 percent of operating revenues, went up by 48.6 percent to 3.689 billion pesos for the first nine months of 1996 from 2.483 billion pesos ... as a result of higher call volumes," the company said.
International calls, which represent 56.3 percent of PLDT's operating revenues, grew by 8.2 percent to 11.908 billion pesos from 11.002 billion pesos last year.

The increase was due to "the combined effects of an increase in call volumes, particularly outgoing calls, a slight depreciation of the Philippine peso relative to the U.S. dollar...", the company said.
Operating expenses expanded marginally by 4.2 percent to 12.830 billion pesos from 12.311 billion pesos.

"This slight increase was attributable to higher depreciation charges and improved employees' benefits, both partially offset by lower expenses in providing customer services and lower operating taxes resulting from the elimination of the 3.0 percent franchise tax," it added.
Other expenses ballooned by 58.2 percent to 1.414 billion pesos from 894 million pesos due to increased borrowings, the company said.
